result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers quote the specific near-duplicate values well. A does better at separating accidental differences from intentional ones: it calls the blue and grey merges invisible, the radius and spacing changes visible, and treats the modal as the real elevation step. It is also more concise and says it only saw one excerpt. B is solid and concrete, but it states contrast ratios while assuming a white background. It also contradicts itself on which step is most visible, and it adds scope (focus/hover states) that the excerpt gives no basis for. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers find the near-duplicate colors and the unscaled radii and spacing, and both quote exact values. B does better at telling accidents apart from intentional differences: it calls the modal the one real elevation step and says which merges won't be noticed (the blues and greys) and which will (radius and spacing). Its order is also better: inventory first, then tokens, then components, with lint rules added early. A's contrast figure is roughly right, but it assumes a white background the excerpt never shows. A also flags missing hover and focus states it has no way to see, and it calls two different steps 'most visible', which contradicts itself.
